children: on Sunday said an experimental immunotherapy combination reduced a blood marker of prostate cancer activity by at least half in 11 of 15 patients receiving the recommended regimen in an early-stage trial. The treatment combines pasritamig and JNJ-9401 in patients whose cancer has spread and continues to progress despite hormone-targeting treatments.

For investors, the results provide an early signal supporting J&J’s ongoing Phase 3 development program in advanced prostate cancer. However, the small study does not establish whether the combination extends survival or works better than existing treatments. Reductions in prostate-specific antigen, or PSA, do not by themselves prove those benefits.

The two drugs are bispecific antibodies, engineered proteins that each bind to two targets. Pasritamig connects immune cells called T cells with cancer cells carrying a protein called KLK2. JNJ-9401 targets another prostate cancer protein, PSMA, while providing an additional signal intended to strengthen the immune attack.

Among the 15 patients, seven achieved PSA reductions of at least 90%, including four whose PSA became undetectable. All seven remained on treatment for more than six months without disease progression. Patients in this group had received a median of four previous drug-treatment regimens.

No severe or life-threatening treatment-related adverse events were reported at the recommended regimen. Three patients experienced mild cytokine release syndrome, an inflammatory reaction caused by immune activation, presenting as temporary fever. No cases of a treatment-associated neurological syndrome were reported.

The regimen involves an injection of JNJ-9401 and an intravenous infusion of pasritamig every six weeks, following two initial weekly doses of pasritamig that gradually increase treatment exposure. The study administers treatment in an outpatient setting.

The overall Phase 1 trial had enrolled 144 patients as of June 15, but the highlighted results concern only the 15 receiving the recommended regimen. The ongoing Phase 3 KLK2-comPAS study is evaluating whether adding JNJ-9401 improves outcomes compared with pasritamig alone.

title: J&J prostate cancer combination lowers PSA in small early study
